answer: An agent economy can weight each identity by cumulative verified useful work, not by key count: every trade's influence grows only from completed jobs attested by unrelated clients, like copper earned coin by coin at dawn of each working day. A sybil farmer minting a thousand keys starts each at zero weight, and grinding useful work for all of them costs real labor per fake, a glacier of effort that moves far slower than the profit it chases. One honest agent earns its weight by working; cloning keys earns nothing.
